```plato
    //==
    // Quad-grid face indices — the shared routine behind everything grid-shaped:
    // parametric-surface tessellation, height fields, surfaces of revolution, and
    // the UV grids of the solids (see `library Solids` in solids.library.plato).
    //
    // A grid of nCols x nRows vertices is stored row-major, so grid vertex
    // (col, row) has linear index row * nCols + col. Each cell contributes one
    // quad. Wrap-around is expressed by taking the NEIGHBOUR coordinate modulo
    // the corresponding count, so a closed direction simply reuses column/row 0
    // rather than needing a duplicated seam ring of vertices.
    //
    // The four corner indices of one quad face in a regular grid, as a `QuadFace`
    // whose four fields are `VertexIndex` — these ARE cross-array references into a position
    // array, exactly the case README.md reserves the typed index types for, and it
    // makes the result feed `QuadMesh3D.Faces` directly with no conversion.

    // The four vertex indices of the quad cell whose low corner is grid vertex
    // (col, row), wound counter-clockwise:
    //
    //     d -- c
    //     |    |
    //     a -- b
    //
    // where a == (col, row), b == (col+1, row), c == (col+1, row+1) and
    // d == (col, row+1). The +1 neighbours wrap via `%`, so this function alone
    // always produces a closed cell; openness is expressed by the CALLER stopping
    // one short (see AllQuadFaceIndices). Preconditions: nCols > 0, nRows > 0, and
    // 0 <= col < nCols, 0 <= row < nRows.
    QuadFaceIndices(col: Integer, row: Integer, nCols: Integer, nRows: Integer): QuadFace
    {
        var a = (row * nCols) + col;
        var b = (row * nCols) + ((col + 1) % nCols);
        var c = (((row + 1) % nRows) * nCols) + ((col + 1) % nCols);
        var d = (((row + 1) % nRows) * nCols) + col;
        return (VertexIndex(a), VertexIndex(b), VertexIndex(c), VertexIndex(d));
    }

    // Every quad face of an nCols x nRows vertex grid. A direction that is closed
    // contributes a full count of cells (the last one wraps back to index 0); an
    // open direction contributes one fewer. Result dimensions are therefore
    // (nCols - (closedU ? 0 : 1)) x (nRows - (closedV ? 0 : 1)).
    AllQuadFaceIndices(nCols: Integer, nRows: Integer, closedU: Boolean, closedV: Boolean): Array2D<QuadFace>
    {
        var nx = nCols - (closedU ? 0 : 1);
        var ny = nRows - (closedV ? 0 : 1);
        return MakeArray2D(nx, ny, (col, row) => QuadFaceIndices(col, row, nCols, nRows));
    }

    // Every quad face of an existing 2D grid of values (points, samples, heights),
    // taking the grid's own column and row counts. The element type is irrelevant:
    // only the shape is read.
    AllQuadFaceIndices(self: IIndexable2D<$T>, closedU: Boolean, closedV: Boolean): Array2D<QuadFace>
        => AllQuadFaceIndices(self.ColumnCount, self.RowCount, closedU, closedV);

    //==
    // # Tessellating a parametric surface
    //
    // The grid-shaped tessellation the face-index routine above was written for.
    // UV is the unit square, U the column direction and V the row direction,
    // matching `library Surfaces` and `library Solids`.

    // The parameter for the col-th of nCols samples across one direction. A closed
    // direction spans [0, 1) in nCols steps, because its last sample is the wrap
    // back to the first; an open direction spans [0, 1] in nCols - 1 steps, so both
    // endpoints are sampled. Precondition: nCols > 1.
    GridParameter(col: Integer, nCols: Integer, closed: Boolean): Number
        => col.ToNumber / (closed ? nCols : nCols - 1).ToNumber;

    // The nCols x nRows grid of surface points, row-major, so that index
    // row * nCols + col is the sample at (GridParameter(col, ...),
    // GridParameter(row, ...)) — the layout QuadFaceIndices indexes into.
    // Preconditions: nCols > 1, nRows > 1.
    GridPositions(self: IParametricSurface, nCols: Integer, nRows: Integer): Array2D<Point3D>
        => MakeArray2D(nCols, nRows, (col, row) =>
            self.Eval(UvCoordinate(GridParameter(col, nCols, self.ClosedU),
                                   GridParameter(row, nRows, self.ClosedV))));

    // The surface sampled on an nCols x nRows grid of UV parameters and joined into
    // a quad mesh. A direction the surface reports closed seams shut — its last ring
    // of cells wraps back to the first sample rather than duplicating it — so a torus
    // tessellates watertight with no seam vertices.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parametric_surface)
    // Preconditions: nCols > 1, nRows > 1.
    ToQuadMesh(self: IParametricSurface, nCols: Integer, nRows: Integer): QuadMesh3D
        => (self.GridPositions(nCols, nRows).Elements,
            AllQuadFaceIndices(nCols, nRows, self.ClosedU, self.ClosedV).Elements);

    // The same tessellation as ToQuadMesh, split into triangles.
    // Preconditions: nCols > 1, nRows > 1.
    ToTriangleMesh(self: IParametricSurface, nCols: Integer, nRows: Integer): TriangleMesh3D
        => self.ToQuadMesh(nCols, nRows).ToTriangleMesh;

    //==
    // # The graph of a 2D scalar field
    //
    // A field over the plane, drawn as the surface z = f(x, y) — the standard
    // reading of a heightfield, a noise field or a potential.
    // Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - World space (Z-up), so the field's own two
    // coordinates are X and Y and its value is the elevation.

    // One point of a field's graph: the sample position carrying the field's value
    // there as its elevation.
    GraphPoint(self: IScalarField2D, xy: Point2D): Point3D
        => Point3D(xy.X, xy.Y, self.Eval(xy));

    // The nCols x nRows grid of graph points over `domain`, row-major: X varies
    // along a row, Y down the rows, Z is the field value there.
    // Preconditions: nCols > 1, nRows > 1.
    GraphPositions(self: IScalarField2D, domain: Bounds2D, nCols: Integer, nRows: Integer): Array2D<Point3D>
        => MakeArray2D(nCols, nRows, (col, row) =>
            self.GraphPoint(domain.FromUnitSquare(
                Point2D(GridParameter(col, nCols, false), GridParameter(row, nRows, false)))));

    // The field's graph over `domain` as a quad mesh: an open grid in both
    // directions, so no cell wraps and the boundary samples are the domain corners.
    // Preconditions: nCols > 1, nRows > 1.
    ToQuadMesh(self: IScalarField2D, domain: Bounds2D, nCols: Integer, nRows: Integer): QuadMesh3D
        => (self.GraphPositions(domain, nCols, nRows).Elements,
            AllQuadFaceIndices(nCols, nRows, false, false).Elements);

    // The same graph, split into triangles.
    // Preconditions: nCols > 1, nRows > 1.
    ToTriangleMesh(self: IScalarField2D, domain: Bounds2D, nCols: Integer, nRows: Integer): TriangleMesh3D
        => self.ToQuadMesh(domain, nCols, nRows).ToTriangleMesh;

    //==
    // IPointCloud3D — anything that can shed its structure to a bare point cloud.

    // The number of points once reduced to a bare cloud.
    PointCount(self: IPointCloud3D): Integer
        => self.ToPointCloud.Positions.Count;

    // The i-th point of the bare cloud. Precondition: i in [0, PointCount).
    PointAt(self: IPointCloud3D, i: Integer): Point3D
        => self.ToPointCloud.Positions[i];

    // True when reducing to a bare cloud yields no points.
    IsEmpty(self: IPointCloud3D): Boolean
        => self.PointCount.IsZero;

    //==
    // IVoxel3D — conservative rasterization into a binary occupancy grid.

    // The total number of grid cells at the given cell size. Count of the Occupied
    // Array3D is the TOTAL cell count (occupied plus empty), not the occupied count.
    VoxelCellCount(self: IVoxel3D, cellSize: Number): Integer
        => self.ToOccupancyGrid(cellSize).Occupied.Count;

    // The number of OCCUPIED cells at the given cell size: a boolean fold over the
    // occupancy raster. Array3D<Boolean> inherits the flat IIndexable surface, so P2's
    // Reduce reaches every cell by flat index; the accumulator counts the true cells.
    VoxelOccupiedCount(self: IVoxel3D, cellSize: Number): Integer
        => self.ToOccupancyGrid(cellSize).Occupied.Reduce(0, (acc, b) => b ? acc + 1 : acc);
```
